diagnosis.summary: You are experiencing poor maize harvests from your shamba in the Webuye area.
likely_causes: Your soil may be too acidic and depleted of nutrients from planting maize in the same spot every year.
The destructive Striga weed, locally known as Kayongo, might be sucking nutrients from your maize roots.
Pests like the Fall Armyworm or stemborers may have damaged your crop during the growing season.
diagnosis.recommended_approach: To fix this, mix plenty of organic manure into your soil and rotate your maize with beans or groundnuts next season.

this_week_actions: Pull up and burn any visible purple-flowered Striga weeds before they shed seeds.
Collect well-decomposed animal manure from your cowshed or purchase it locally.
Dig and mix two handfuls of the manure into each planting hole to enrich your soil.
Visit the local agro-dealer to buy certified bean seeds for your upcoming crop rotation.
materials_needed: Dry, well-decomposed cattle or poultry manure.
Certified bean seeds for the next planting season.
A standard hand hoe for mixing manure into the soil.
warning_signs: Maize leaves show ragged holes with wet, sawdust-like waste inside the center whorl.
Maize plants remain severely stunted and pale yellow even after adding manure.
action_plan.expected_outcome: By the next harvest season, you can expect healthier green maize stalks and an increased crop yield.
